name: @atlasbound/decisionbook
description: DecisionBook: the history of why beside git's history of what, as plain append-only files a team commits; a readiness rubric, a gate, resume.

verbs.what: choose which files need a plan you approve before an AI session edits them: protect <path or glob>[,...]; with no word, what you could choose

help.when: once, when setup asks; again whenever you want to protect more
help.changes: .decisionbook/config.json: commit it, so your team shares the same protection

flags.--source: protect the source folders and entry files it found
flags.--none: protect nothing (takes protection away: you only, after the phrase)

verbs.what: how planning before code works: your AI session starts a plan with /decisionbook, you answer its questions and approve

<record>, --file <draft in .atlasbound/drafts/> (removed once written), or the JSON on standard input: start a plan: {"title", "why", "success", "kind", "level": micro|normal|critical, "records": [<record>, ...]}; says the state it left

help.line: start a plan for a task (your AI session does this in /decisionbook)
help.when: before code changes a protected file
help.changes: a plan file in .decisionbook/ (commit it with the code)

flags.--file <path>: read the JSON from this draft in .atlasbound/drafts/, then remove it

verbs.what: <id> <record> | <id> [<record>, ...], --file <draft in .atlasbound/drafts/> (removed once written), or the JSON on standard input: append one record, or a JSON array of them in one call, all or none: research (a run probe too), a question, a decision, an assumption, the person's confirm, a check, an item (a step too), a link, a waiver, a note; READY when complete, says the state

help.line: add what the plan learned or settled: research, a question, a decision, a check, a step
help.when: while the plan is made, one record or several at once

flags.--file <path>: read the JSON from this draft in .atlasbound/drafts/, then remove it

verbs.what: <id>: READY at the level code decides, else each missing row

help.line: say whether a plan is complete enough to build from (READY), or what it still needs
help.when: after the plan has its decisions and checks
help.changes: marks the plan READY when it is complete

verbs.what: <id> [node...] | <type:value>: one plan (in full once a session, then its node map; a node: field[.key|order|index]), or a file, decision, issue, test or commit with its links both ways

help.line: show a plan, or what the plans say about a file, a decision or a commit
help.when: to read a plan or why a file is the way it is

flags.--full: the whole plan, not its map

help.line: find the plans that mention some words
help.when: to look up an earlier decision

verbs.what: <path|words>: the earlier plans of an area: the files, their folder and imports, the same concerns

help.line: list earlier plans that touched the same files or area
help.when: before a new plan, to reuse what was decided

verbs.what: <path|words>: the plan pack of an area: its binding decisions, assumptions no person confirmed, check commands, files, the level and what READY needs there, the two calls

help.line: gather what an area already settled, so a new plan starts from it

verbs.what: what a new session on this branch receives

help.line: show what a new AI session on this branch is told: settled decisions, open questions
help.when: to see what the next session inherits

verbs.what: what waits for you: a draft's open questions with the answer proposed, READY plans not closed, plans set aside; on this branch, then in the plans pulled from other branches

help.line: list what waits for you: open questions, READY plans not closed, plans set aside
help.when: at the start of a day, or before you switch work

verbs.what: <file>[:<line>]: git blame names the commit, the closed plan that lists it says why: its decisions in the person's words and what replaced each since; an unknown is said, never guessed

help.line: say why a line is the way it is: its commit, the plan that shipped it, the person's decisions
help.when: before you change code someone decided

verbs.what: [<id> | --branch]: a pull request description in Markdown from the plan records (goal, the person's decisions in their words, what their questions proposed, checks, commits); printed, nothing sent

help.line: write a pull request description from a plan's records, never from a chat
help.when: when you open a pull request for the work

flags.--branch: every plan of this branch but one set aside or replaced (the default)

verbs.what: <id>: record what shipped: its own commits, files and tests

help.line: record what shipped for a plan: its commits, files and tests
help.when: when the work of a plan is done

verbs.what: READY or not, and why. The plan-before-code part answers it; an install without that part says package-not-installed

help.line: say whether this branch's plan is READY, and why not
help.when: when a check held a write

verbs.what: the plan part the next session on this branch would receive (settled decisions, open questions). An install without the plan-before-code part says package-not-installed

help.line: show the plan part the next session on this branch would get
help.when: to see what a new session inherits

next.what: choose what needs a plan before an AI session edits it
